property_summary: After any call to Put, the contract's Ether balance equals the sum of all deposited msg.values, because the reference adds msg.value to the user's balance, while the buggy version adds zero, causing the contract's balance to exceed the sum of users' balances by the amount deposited.

After a Put call, the sum over all Acc balances is at least the contract's own Ether balance, but the bug causes deposited value to be lost from user balances, so the sum will eventually fall short of the contract's balance.
After a Put call, the caller's Acc balance increases by at least the msg.value sent, but the buggy version adds zero instead.
After a Put call, the caller's Acc balance must increase by the amount of Ether sent, but the buggy version adds zero, causing the balance to remain unchanged.
For any Put call, the sum of all Acc balances after the call equals the sum before plus msg.value; the bug adds zero instead, so the sum increases by less than msg.value.

After a Put call, the contract's balance should increase by the sent value; the bug violates this by not updating the user's balance, so the contract balance exceeds the user's recorded balance by at least the sent value.
After a Put call, Acc[msg.sender].balance must be at least msg.value; the bug version leaves it at zero, so the property fails.
After Put is called with a value, the caller's recorded balance in Acc must be strictly greater than before the call; the buggy version never updates the balance, so it remains unchanged.

After Put is called with some value, the total of all recorded balances in Acc must equal the contract's balance plus the initial total balances; the buggy version never updates the balance, so the recorded total falls short of the contract's balance.

The sum of all individual account balances held in the Acc mapping plus the contract's own ether balance must equal the total amount ever deposited; the reentrant version can cause this invariant to be violated because a reentrant Put can inflate a single account's balance without a net new deposit to the contract.
After any number of Put calls, each holder's balance should equal the sum of msg.value they have sent via Put; reentrancy can inflate a holder's balance beyond their actual deposits.

After any sequence of Put calls, the sum of all Acc balances equals the contract's ether balance; reentrancy allows a single Put to increase a single account's balance multiple times, breaking this equality.
After a reentrant Put call that invokes itself via fallback, the caller's Acc balance will exceed the sum of msg.value received in the outermost Put call.

After any put, the contract's total Ether balance equals the sum of all acc balances, but the buggy version allows reentrant collection during the same Put to withdraw without updating the balance, breaking this invariant.

After a single call to Put by any sender, the sender's Acc balance is exactly the sum of its prior balance and the msg.value sent, but the buggy version allows reentrant collection within Put that can withdraw funds without updating the balance, breaking this invariant.

After any external call to C, the invariant that sum of Acc[addr].balance over all addresses ever interacted with equals address(c).balance holds for the reference, but the buggy version allows reentrant collect during Put that transfers ETH without updating the balance, breaking this invariant for at least one input the fuzzer finds.
After a Put call completes, the Acc balance of the caller is at least msg.value, but the buggy version allows reentrant Collect within the fallback that can reduce the balance below this amount.
After a Put call completes, Acc[caller].balance is non-decreasing relative to its pre-Put value, but the buggy version allows reentrant Collect within the fallback that can reduce the balance.
Collect should revert if called before the unlock time.
Calling Collect must always revert in the test scenario.
Collect must revert when called with a positive _am and unlock time in the future, even after a zero-value Put.
Collect reverts when called with a positive amount after a zero-value Put with a future unlock time.
Collect must revert when called after a zero-value Put with a future unlock time if the contract holds no balance for the test account.

In P, a Collect call only succeeds if block.timestamp > acc.unlockTime; in M, a Collect call can succeed even when block.timestamp <= acc.unlockTime, violating the invariant that funds cannot be withdrawn before the unlock time.

In the reference contract, a Collect call that would transfer Ether can never succeed when block.timestamp is less than or equal to the account's unlockTime; the mutant breaks this rule by allowing a successful transfer even when block.timestamp <= acc.unlockTime.

In the reference, a Collect call that transfers Ether can only succeed if block.timestamp > acc.unlockTime; the mutant allows success even when block.timestamp <= acc.unlockTime, breaking the time-lock invariant.

In the reference, a Collect call that transfers Ether can only succeed if the account's unlockTime has passed; the mutant allows a successful transfer even when block.timestamp is less than or equal to the unlockTime.

In the reference, a Collect call with _am>0 that does not revert always leaves the caller's balance reduced by exactly _am and the caller's unlockTime strictly less than block.timestamp; the mutant allows a balance reduction even when block.timestamp <= acc.unlockTime.
After a successful Collect, the contract's Ether balance must decrease by the collected amount.

property_summary: After a successful Collect, the user's recorded balance must decrease by the collected amount; the bug skips the deduction so the balance remains unchanged.

After any call to Collect that does not revert, the sum of all Acc balances plus the contract's ether balance must equal the total Ether ever deposited via Put or the fallback; the bug violates this because it fails to reduce the user's balance after transferring Ether.
